#Paper 1


## Participants

A total of 616 participants were recruited from Amazon Mechanical Turk (MTurk). MTurk allows researchers to collect high-quality data rapidly among demographically diverse individuals \cite{buhrmesterAmazonMechanicalTurk2011}. Prior work has shown that MTurk can be reliably used to make inferences about a number of broader populations of interest \cite{coppockGeneralizingSurveyExperiments2019, huffWhoAreThese2015, johnsonAmazonMechanicalTurk2020}. The participants were required to be located within the United States, over the age of 18, fluent in English. While limitations apply the MTurk studies (see Limitations in the Discussion), studies have shown that the quality of MTurk responses can improve with \textit{a priori} researcher constraints \cite{peerReputationSufficientCondition2014, cheungAmazonMechanicalTurk2017, thomasValidityMechanicalTurk2017}. In the current study, we required that participants had previously completed at least 100 tasks and maintained at least a 95\% approval rating on MTurk. We additionally applied exclusions to further ensure that we analyzed high-quality behavioral data (see Exclusions). Our final sample was `r sample`participants.The total sample consisted of `r n.female` females, $M_{age}$ = `r mage` years of age ($SD_{age}$ = `r sdage`), with `r n.HighSchool` high school, `r n.Undergraduate` undergraduate, and `r n.Postgraduate` postgraduate, and identified as White/Caucasian (*n* = `r n.white`), Asian (*n* = `r n.asian`), Hispanic/Latino (*n* = `r n.hispanic`), Black/African American (*n* = `r n.black`), Pacific Islander (*n* = `r n.pacific`) other/multiple (*n* = `r n.othereth`), or did not disclose their ethnicity (*n* = `r n.notreported`). The included subjects completed the task in an average of $M_{task}$ = `r mtask` minutes ($SD_{task}$ = `r sdtask`) and the survey in an average of $M_{survey}$ = `r msurvey` minutes ($SD_{survey}$ = `r sdsurvey`).

## Exlclusion Criteria

In line with recommendations for studies conducted using Amazons Mechanical Turk (AMT) service, careful instructions and \textit{a priori} exclusion criteria were applied to further ensure data quality \cite{crumpEvaluatingAmazonMechanical2013}. Using a multi-method approach to detect careless/invalid responses in online samples, several data exclusion criteria were applied \cite{curranMethodsDetectionCarelessly2016}. A total of `r excluded` participants were excluded. Participants single trials were excluded if response times were either 250 milli-seconds or above 90 seconds. Given that participants had ample time to respond to each question (up to as long until they made a decision), we reasoned that these participants were not devoting sufficient attention to the task. Additionally, having considered trial wise exclusions, participants were also excluded for failure to complete at least 40 trials in the specified range. Finally, participants were excluded for failure of passing four attention check items and a total survey completion time below five minutes. Because our survey battery involved 11 different assessments, we reasoned that a total completion time below five minutes reflected a careless responder. Our overall exclusion rate of `r exlclusion_rate`\% is well in line with research findings studying quality control measures on MTurk \cite{crumpEvaluatingAmazonMechanical2013, downsAreYourParticipants2010, paolacciTurkUnderstandingMechanical2014}.

##Risk and Benefits
```{r get the eBLUPs}
GLMM_data <- Neuroethics_Judgement %>% 
  mutate(dominate = ifelse(Yes >= 75 *.90 | No >= 75 *.90, "dominate", "not_dominate")) %>% 
  filter(!dominate == "dominate") %>% select(user_id, condition, risk, gain, experimental_treatment_selected) %>% mutate(experimental_treatment_selected = ifelse(experimental_treatment_selected == "Yes to treatment", 1, 0)) %>% 
  group_by(user_id) %>%
  mutate(risk = scale(risk),
         gain = scale(gain)) %>% 
  ungroup()

#within subject scaling used here
#here is the first model
glmm.1 <- glmer(experimental_treatment_selected ~ risk + gain +
               (risk + gain | user_id), 
             data = GLMM_data, family = binomial(link="logit"), 
             control=glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa"),
             nAGQ = 1)
#extract the eblups
eblups <- do.call(rbind.data.frame, ranef(glmm.1)) %>%
  rownames_to_column() %>%
  mutate(user_id = factor(str_remove(rowname, "user_id."))) %>%
  mutate(Intercept = `(Intercept)` + fixef(glmm.1)[["(Intercept)"]],
         risk = risk + fixef(glmm.1)[["risk"]],
         gain = gain + fixef(glmm.1)[["gain"]]) %>%
  select(-rowname, -`(Intercept)`) %>% 
  left_join(dplyr::select(data.h, user_id, condition), by = "user_id") %>% distinct()

se <- sqrt(diag(vcov(glmm.1)))
# table of estimates with 95% CI
(tab <- cbind(Est = fixef(glmm.1), LL = fixef(glmm.1) - 1.96 * se, UL = fixef(glmm.1) + 1.96 * se))
exp(tab)

broomExtra::tidy(glmm.1)
broomExtra::glance(glmm.1)

#test for difference between parameters.
#(0.3134202) -  (-0.2497197)
car::linearHypothesis(glmm.1, "gain + risk = 0")
```

**##Statistical test for risk vs. benefit**
```{r testing for risk & benefit difference}
eblups %>% 
  select(user_id, condition, risk, gain) %>% 
  reshape2::melt(id = c("user_id", "condition") , variable.name = "type", value.name = "subject_specific_effect") -> test 

test$user_id <- factor(test$user_id)

test$subject_specific_effect <- abs(test$subject_specific_effect)

t <- t.test(subject_specific_effect ~ type,  paired = TRUE, alternative = "two.sided", conf.level = 0.95,var.equal = F, data =test)
tab <- map_df(list(t), tidy)
knitr::kable(tab[c("estimate", "statistic", "p.value", "parameter", "conf.low", 
"conf.high", "method")], caption = "Parired T-test")%>%  
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")

# plot
tt <- ggstatsplot::ggwithinstats(
  data = test,
  x = type,
  y = subject_specific_effect,
  title = "Paired t-test of the participant specific risk and benifit sensitivity",
  ylab = "Individual-level random slope coefficients",
  xlab = "sensitivity",
  subtitle = "",
  caption = "",
  ggstatsplot.layer = T,
  point.path = F,
  point.args = list(size = 3, alpha = 0.4, position = "jitter", width = 0.2),
  mean.plotting = T,
  effsize.type = "d",
  nboot = 1000L,
    bf.message = F,
)

test %>% 
  group_by(type) %>% 
  summarise(
    median = median(subject_specific_effect),
    mean = mean(subject_specific_effect),
    sd = sd(subject_specific_effect)
  )
```

**##Interdomain stability**
```{r cog domain h2, echo=FALSE}
eblups %>% 
  select(user_id, condition, risk, gain)  -> test 

test %>% 
  group_by(condition) %>% 
  summarise(
    eBLUPs_risk = mean(risk),
    sd_risk = sd(risk),
    eBLUPs_gain = mean(gain),
    sd_gain = sd(gain)
 ) %>% 
  kable(digits=3) %>% kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")

aov.1 <- stats::oneway.test(risk ~ condition, data = test, var.equal= T)
aov.2 <- stats::oneway.test(gain ~ condition, data = test, var.equal= T)

aov_p1 <- ggstatsplot::ggbetweenstats(data = test,
  x = condition,
  y = risk,
  title = "Risk sensitivity across cognitive domains",
    ylab = "Individual-level random slope coefficients",
  xlab = "Cognitve Domain",
    pairwise.comparisons = F,
  bf.message = F
)+theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

aov_p2 <- ggstatsplot::ggbetweenstats(data = test,
  x = condition,
  y = gain,
  title = "Benefit sensitivity across cognitive domains",
  ylab = "Individual-level random slope coefficients",
  xlab = "Cognitve Domain",
    pairwise.comparisons = F,
  bf.message = F)+theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

aov_p1+ aov_p2

#create a table 
tab <- map_df(list(aov.1,aov.2), tidy)
knitr::kable(tab[c("num.df", "den.df", "statistic", "p.value", "method")], caption = "one way anova testing cognitve domain; (Risk and Gain)")%>%  
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")

#GLMM_data$condition <- relevel(GLMM_data$condition, "Motor Function")

glmm.cog <- glmer(experimental_treatment_selected ~ risk + gain + condition +
               (risk + gain | user_id), 
             data = GLMM_data, family = binomial(link="logit"), 
             control=glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa"),
             nAGQ = 1, contrasts = list(condition = contr.sum))

summary(glmm.cog)
```

The model `glmm.cog` suggests that individuals in the motor function condition are significantly more likely to recommend the treatment option. While the effects of risk and benefits do not change this main effect of the motor function condition indicates that individuals will recommend treatment for motor dysfunction versus cognition. 

```{r look for best fitting model analysis}
cl <- makeCluster(8)
clusterEvalQ(cl, require(lme4))
#start with risk, and gain

glmm.1 <- glmer(experimental_treatment_selected ~ risk + gain +
               (risk + gain | user_id), 
             data = GLMM_data, family = binomial(link="logit"), 
             control=glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa"),
             nAGQ = 1)

#add poly gain
glmm.2 <- glmer(experimental_treatment_selected ~ risk + gain + I(gain^2) +
               (risk + gain | user_id), 
             data = GLMM_data, family = binomial(link="logit"), 
             control=glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa"),
             nAGQ = 1)

#just add poly risk 
glmm.3 <- glmer(experimental_treatment_selected ~ risk + gain + I(gain^2) + I(risk^2) +
               (risk + gain | user_id), 
             data = GLMM_data, family = binomial(link="logit"), 
             control=glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa"),
             nAGQ = 1)

#linear interaction
glmm.4 <- glmer(experimental_treatment_selected ~ risk + gain + I(gain^2) + I(risk^2) +
                  risk:gain+
               (risk + gain | user_id), 
             data = GLMM_data, family = binomial(link="logit"), 
             control=glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa"),
             nAGQ = 1)

#add risk gain^2 interaction
glmm.5 <- glmer(experimental_treatment_selected ~ risk + gain + I(gain^2) + I(risk^2) +
                  risk:gain +
                  risk:I(gain^2) +
               (risk + gain | user_id), 
             data = GLMM_data, family = binomial(link="logit"), 
             control=glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa"),
             nAGQ = 1)

#add gain risk^2 interaction
glmm.6 <- glmer(experimental_treatment_selected ~ risk + gain + I(gain^2) + I(risk^2) +
                  risk:gain+
                  risk:I(gain^2) +
                  gain:I(risk^2) +
               (risk + gain | user_id), 
             data = GLMM_data, family = binomial(link="logit"), 
             control=glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa"),
             nAGQ = 1)

#add polynomial interaction
glmm.7 <- glmer(experimental_treatment_selected ~ risk + gain + I(gain^2) + I(risk^2) +
                  risk:gain+
                  risk:I(gain^2) +
                  gain:I(risk^2) + 
                  I(risk^2):I(gain^2)+
               (risk + gain | user_id), 
             data = GLMM_data, family = binomial(link="logit"), 
             control=glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa"),
             nAGQ = 1)

table <-anova(glmm.1, glmm.2, glmm.3, glmm.4, glmm.5, glmm.6, glmm.7)
tab <- map_df(list(table), tidy)
options(knitr.kable.NA = '')
knitr::kable(tab[c("term", "npar", "AIC", "BIC", "logLik", "deviance", "statistic", 
                   "df", "p.value")], caption = "Model Comparison", digits = 3)%>%  
  kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position")

stopCluster(cl)

performance::compare_performance(glmm.1, glmm.2, glmm.3, glmm.4, glmm.5, glmm.6, glmm.7, rank = T)
```

**Table 1:** main effects for logistic regression with random effects

*Note:* Standardized parameters were obtained by fitting the model on a standardized version of the dataset. 95% Confidence Intervals (CIs) and p-values were computed using Satterthwaite approximation.

```{r}
RROO <- glmer(experimental_treatment_selected ~ risk + gain + I(gain^2) + I(risk^2) +
                  risk:gain+
                  risk:I(gain^2) +
                  gain:I(risk^2) + condition +
               (risk + gain | user_id), 
             data = GLMM_data, family = binomial(link="logit"), 
             control=glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa"),
             nAGQ = 1, contrasts = list(condition = contr.sum))

plot(ggeffects::ggpredict(RROO, terms=c("condition [all]")))+
  geom_hline(yintercept = abs(fixef(glmm.6)[1]), linetype = "dashed")+
  labs(
    x = "Condition", 
    y = "Probability of recommending treatment", 
    color = "Domain",
    title = "Predicting Treatment Recommendation by Cogntive Domain"
  )+
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(.25,.5),label = scales::percent)+
  theme_classic()+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = .58))
```
The model `glmm.cog` suggests that individuals in the motor function condition are significantly more likely to recommend the treatment option than the average predicted probability of recommending the treatment (represented by the dashed line). While the effects of risk and benefits do not change this main effect of the motor function condition indicates that individuals will recommend treatment for motor dysfunction versus cognition.

```{r education data, echo=FALSE}
  inner_join(data.h) %>% 
  filter(! user_id == "RU3gTWzp") %>% 
  mutate(education = fct_recode(education,
  HighSchool = "high school degree",
  Undergraduate = "bachelor",
```

#suppTable S3 

Generalized linear modeling results using the "lme4" package (R
version x.X.X; “lme4” version X.X-XX).

For each state the model formula, results and fixed effect terms: 
```{r supp}

get_model_stuff <- function(model){
  stuff <- list() 
  x <- summary(model)
  formula = x[["call"]]
  stuff[[1]] = toString(formula)
  results = broom.mixed::glance(model) %>% select(AIC, BIC, logLik, deviance, df.residual)
  stuff[[2]] = results
  terms   = broom.mixed::tidy(model) %>% filter(effect == "fixed") %>% 
  select(term, estimate, std.error, statistic, p.value)
  stuff[[3]] = terms
  return(stuff)
}
models <- c(glmm.1, glmm.2, glmm.3, glmm.4, glmm.5, glmm.6, glmm.7)

models %>% 
map(get_model_stuff) -> supp
kable(supp) #we are on to something here! 
```

```{r individual difference analysis (interactions instead)}
GLMM_data <- Neuroethics_Judgement %>% 
  mutate(dominate = ifelse(Yes >= 75 *.90 | No >= 75 *.90, "dominate", "not_dominate")) %>% 
  filter(!dominate == "dominate") %>% select(user_id, condition, risk, gain, experimental_treatment_selected, age, sex, Income, education) %>% mutate(experimental_treatment_selected = ifelse(experimental_treatment_selected == "Yes to treatment", 1, 0)) %>% 
  group_by(user_id) %>%
  mutate(risk = scale(risk),
         gain = scale(gain)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  filter(! sex == "Other") %>%# only have 3 people who reported other as sex
  mutate(sex = factor(sex)) %>% 
  filter(!Income == 0) %>% 
  mutate(Income = log(Income)) %>% 
  filter(! user_id == "RU3gTWzp") %>% 
  mutate(education = fct_recode(education,
  HighSchool = "high school degree",
  Undergraduate = "bachelor",
  Postgraduate = "masters",
  Postgraduate = "Doctoral/Professional"
)) %>% #we only have a single subject less than high school 
  mutate(education = factor(education),
         age = scale(age),
         Income = scale(Income))

GLMM_data$education <- relevel(GLMM_data$education, "HighSchool")

individual_diff <- glmer(experimental_treatment_selected ~ (risk + gain)*education + condition + risk*age + gain*sex + Income + 
                           (risk + gain | user_id), 
             data = GLMM_data, family = binomial(link="logit"), 
             control=glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa"),
             nAGQ = 1, contrasts = list(condition = contr.sum))

summary(individual_diff)

probe_interaction(individual_diff, pred = risk, modx = gain, mod2 = education,  johnson_neyman = F, confint =TRUE,data = GLMM_data)
probe_interaction(individual_diff, pred = risk, modx = age, johnson_neyman = F, confint =TRUE,data = GLMM_data)
probe_interaction(individual_diff, pred = gain, modx = sex, johnson_neyman = F, confint =TRUE,data = GLMM_data)


library(afex)
cl <- makeCluster(8)
clusterEvalQ(cl, require(afex))
glrMod1.glr <- afex::mixed(experimental_treatment_selected ~ (risk + gain)*(age + sex + Income + education) + condition +
                           (risk + gain | user_id), 
             data = GLMM_data, family = binomial(link="logit"), 
             control=glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa"), method='LRT',
             nAGQ = 1, contrasts = list(condition = contr.sum))
stopCluster(cl)
```

```{r testing nonlinear weighting function}
GLMM_data <- Neuroethics_Judgement %>% 
  mutate(dominate = ifelse(Yes >= 75 *.90 | No >= 75 *.90, "dominate", "not_dominate")) %>% 
  filter(!dominate == "dominate") %>% select(user_id, condition, risk, gain, experimental_treatment_selected) %>% mutate(experimental_treatment_selected = ifelse(experimental_treatment_selected == "Yes to treatment", 1, 0))

#using the weighting function from Lattimore and colleagues 
w <- function(p, delta, gamma) {
  (delta*p^gamma)/(delta*p^gamma + (1 -  p)^gamma)
}
delta = 0.77 #weights from Gonzalez and Wu (1999)
gamma = 0.44

weighted_risk <- w(GLMM_data$risk/100, delta, gamma)
weighted_gain <- w(GLMM_data$gain/100, delta, gamma)

ggplot(data_frame(p = GLMM_data$risk/100, dw = weighted_risk), aes(x = p, y = dw))+
  geom_point(color = "white")+
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1)+theme_classic()+
  geom_smooth(se = F,color = "black")+
  scale_x_continuous(name="", limits=c(0, 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(name="", limits=c(0, 1))
ggplot(data_frame(p = GLMM_data$gain/100, dw = weighted_gain), aes(x = p, y = dw))+
  geom_point(color = "white")+
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1)+theme_classic()+
  geom_smooth(se = F, color = "black")+
  scale_x_continuous(name="", limits=c(0, 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(name="", limits=c(0, 1)) 

 GLMM_data <- Neuroethics_Judgement %>% 
   mutate(dominate = ifelse(Yes >= 75 *.90 | No >= 75 *.90, "dominate", "not_dominate")) %>% 
   filter(!dominate == "dominate") %>% select(user_id, condition, risk, gain, experimental_treatment_selected) %>% mutate(experimental_treatment_selected = ifelse(experimental_treatment_selected == "Yes to treatment", 1, 0)) %>% 
   group_by(user_id) %>%
   mutate(weighted_risk = w(risk/100, delta, gamma),
          weighted_gain = w(gain/100, delta, gamma),
          w_risk = scale(weighted_risk),
          g_gain = scale(weighted_gain)) %>% 
   ungroup()

glmm.1 <- glmer(experimental_treatment_selected ~ w_risk + g_gain +
               (w_risk + g_gain | user_id), 
             data = GLMM_data, family = binomial(link="logit"), 
             control=glmerControl(optimizer="bobyqa"),
             nAGQ = 1)
summary(glmm.1)
broomExtra::glance(glmm.1)
```
